evidence.passage: In this fictional pilot, pump A delivered a mean 0.2 g per actuation with a 0.02 g standard deviation over 20 actuations. Jar B scoops had a 0.08 g standard deviation over 20 scoops. Both used the same test lotion. No user demand or skin outcomes were measured.
limitations: Synthetic test fixture, not real cosmetic product evidence

evidence.passage: Pump A leaked in 3 of 10 simulated transit trials. Jar B leaked in 0 of 10. These small samples cannot establish population failure rates. Packaging redesign and a larger transit test are needed before a shipping claim.
Marketing copy asserts that precise pump dosing proves sensitive-skin safety and universal consumer demand. No tolerance study or consumer research supports this assertion.
limitations: Deliberately unsupported inference in a synthetic evaluation pack
